extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians and graduate students in geometric analysis / Ricci flow
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria, estimates and classification results used to analyze and classify ancient κ-solutions of the Ricci flow (including reduced distance/volume estimates, curvature/volume bounds, blow-up localization lemmas, and classification of shrinking solitons in dimensions 2 and 3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Li–Yau–Perelman distance differential inequalities
rubrics_metrics.description: The reduced distance l (and the approximating ˜l_k) satisfy the differential inequalities (6.2.12)-(6.2.13) (and the rewritten forms (6.2.14)-(6.2.15)), e.g. (˜l_k)_s − Δ˜l_k + (1/(2s))˜l_k − (1/2)|∇˜l_k|^2 + ˜R(k) ≥ 0 and 2Δ˜l_k − |∇˜l_k|^2 + ˜R(k) + (˜l_k − n)/(s) ≤ 0, and the limiting function ¯l satisfies the analogous inequalities in the sense of distributions (6.2.16)-(6.2.17).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These inequalities are used to pass to limits for scaled solutions: gradient estimates (6.2.11) give local uniform bounds so ˜l_k → ¯l in C^{0,α}_loc; the distributional inequalities then imply regularity and further PDE identities for ¯l (leading to soliton identities).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradient estimate for reduced distance (6.2.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: A gradient estimate bounds time-derivative and spatial gradients of ˜l_k: |(˜l_k)_s| + |∇˜l_k|^2 + ˜R(k) ≤ C(s) (schematically as in (6.2.11)), implying local uniform bounds on ˜l_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This estimate implies ˜l_k are uniformly bounded on compact subsets and (up to subsequence) converge to a locally Lipschitz ¯l; together with the distributional PDEs it yields smoothness of ¯l via parabolic theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's reduced volume monotonicity and reduced volume limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Perelman's reduced volume ˜V(s) is monotone (Theorem 3.2.8). For scaled metrics ˜g^{(k)} one gets ˜V^{(k)}(s) monotone and converging along subsequences to a constant ¯V (6.2.18).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monotonicity and Jacobian comparison permit application of dominated convergence to pass to limits. The limit ¯V is used to deduce geometric properties of the limit (for example, ¯V<1 rules out flat R^n limits). Note: the limit ¯V may exceed the reduced volume of the limit manifold if base points diverge to infinity; nevertheless ¯V provides a nontrivial invariant to test flatness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gradient shrinking soliton identity for the limit (6.2.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: If equalities hold in the limiting distributional PDEs then the limit metric ¯g_{ij}(s) and function ¯l satisfy the soliton identity ¯R_{ij} + ∇_i ∇_j ¯l − (1/(2s)) ¯g_{ij} = 0 (equation (6.2.23)), i.e. the limit is a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivation uses the vanishing of the linearized operator applied to v = [s(2Δ¯l + ¯R) + ¯l − n] (4πs)^{-n/2} e^{-¯l} (see (6.2.22)). Once the soliton equation holds, standard regularity shows ¯l is smooth and the limit is a smooth gradient shrinking soliton.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonflatness criterion via reduced volume (< 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a nonflat ancient κ-solution its reduced volume ˜V(τ) satisfies ˜V(τ) < 1 for τ > 0; hence the limiting reduced volume ¯V(s) (from scalings) is strictly less than 1, which excludes a flat R^n soliton as the limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Perelman's Jacobian comparison and the fact that equality ˜V = 1 characterizes Euclidean space; since the ancient κ-solution assumed nonflat, ˜V(τ)<1 and the limit ¯V<1, contradiction if the limit were flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of two-dimensional nonflat ancient κ-solutions (Theorem 6.2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only nonflat ancient κ-solutions to Ricci flow on two-dimensional manifolds are the round sphere S^2 and the round real projective plane RP^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hypotheses used: ancient κ-solution on a 2D manifold with Li–Yau–Hamilton inequality (so scalar curvature is pointwise nondecreasing) and strictly positive curvature. Key steps: scalings converge to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton with bounded curvature, which must be compact and of constant curvature; hence scalings converge to round S^2 or RP^2 and the original solution is round at all times by entropy monotonicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scalar curvature monotonicity/time-nondecreasing property (2D)
rubrics_metrics.description: For ancient κ-solutions (in particular in 2D) the scalar curvature is pointwise nondecreasing in time (Corollary 2.5.8 / Li–Yau–Hamilton inequalities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This property and the strong maximum principle imply strictly positive curvature everywhere for nonflat ancient κ-solutions in 2D, which is used in classification arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scaled entropy E(t) is strictly decreasing unless constant-curvature (6.2.27–6.2.28)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hamilton scaled entropy E(t) = ∫_M R log[R(T − t)] dV_t satisfies dE/dt ≤ 0 and is strictly decreasing along the Ricci flow unless the metric has constant curvature; equality characterizations use identities such as (6.2.28).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining energy computations with Chow's inequality (6.2.28) shows E(t) minimal at round metrics (S^2 or RP^2); this is used to conclude that limits with minimal entropy force the entire ancient solution to have constant curvature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asymptotic volume ratio of ancient κ-solutions is zero (Lemma 6.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (M,g_{ij}(t)) be a nonflat ancient solution with nonnegative curvature operator and bounded curvature. Then the asymptotic volume ratio ν_M(t) = lim_{r→∞} Vol_t(B_t(O,r))/r^n = 0 for each t (Lemma 6.3.1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds by induction on dimension and considers three cases for the asymptotic scalar curvature ratio A (A = ∞, 0 < A < ∞, A = 0), using blow-up arguments, Hamilton compactness, and splitting/de Rham decomposition to obtain contradictions if ν_M(t)>0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization lemma for almost-maximal curvature points (Lemma 6.3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given B>4, C>1000, there exists A large so that: if a solution on M with Bt(x0,1) compactly contained in M admits (x',t') with dt'(x',x0) ≤ 1/4 and |Rm(x',t')| > C + B(t' + t0)^{-1}, then there exists (x̄,t̄) with Q = |Rm(x̄,t̄)| > C + B(t̄ + t0)^{-1} and for all (x,t) with t̄ − A Q^{-1} ≤ t ≤ t̄ and d_t(x,x̄) ≤ (1/10) A^{1/2} Q^{-1/2} we have |Rm(x,t)| ≤ 4Q (plus distance bounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a blow-up localization lemma (Perelman's argument) to find space-time points where curvature is almost maximal and controlled in a parabolic neighborhood; used to take rescaled limits and apply compactness. Constants and neighborhood sizes scale with Q and A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perelman's local curvature estimate from volume lower bound (Theorem 6.3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every w>0 there exist B(w), τ0(w), ξ(w), C(w) such that: if on a solution defined on [t0 − r0^2, t0] the ball B_t(x0,r0) satisfies sectional curvature bound Rm(.,t) ≥ −r0^{-2} and Vol_t(B_t(x0,r0)) ≥ w r0^n at each time, then |Rm(x,t)| ≤ C r0^{-2} + B (t + t0 r0^2)^{-1} whenever t∈[t0−r0^2, t0] and d_t(x,x0) ≤ r0/4. (Part (ii) gives propagation of volume lower bound and similar curvature bounds on a smaller time interval depending on τ0 and ¯τ.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The theorem gives a crucial implication: local lower volume bounds + lower curvature bound imply explicit local curvature upper bounds (decaying like r0^{-2} spatially and (t-shift)^{-1} in time). The proof uses Lemma 6.3.2, blow-up limits, Lemma 6.3.1 (ν=0), and standard comparison/compactness arguments. Constants depend only on w and dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of gradient shrinking Ricci soliton (6.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A solution g_{ij}(t) is a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton if there exists a smooth f such that ∇_i ∇_j f + R_{ij} + (1/(2t)) g_{ij} = 0 for −∞ < t < 0 (equation (6.4.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpretation: the soliton moves by diffeomorphisms generated by ∇f and shrinks homothetically; the soliton equation is the stationary form of the backwards Ricci flow up to diffeomorphism and scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of 3D nonflat κ-noncollapsed shrinking solitons with nonnegative curvature (Lemma 6.4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If (M,g_{ij}(t)) is a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton on a three-manifold with bounded and nonnegative sectional curvature and κ-noncollapsed on all scales, then (i) it is the round S^3 (or a metric quotient of S^3), or (ii) it is the round infinite cylinder S^2 × R or one of its Z_2 quotients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses splitting when curvature is not strictly positive, Hamilton strong maximum principle, pulling back to universal cover, and κ-noncollapsing to rule out compactness failures. The classification is used as an endpoint for blow-up/limit arguments in three dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: κ-noncollapsed on all scales as a standing assumption/useful property
rubrics_metrics.description: A solution is κ-noncollapsed on all scales if every metric ball of radius r with |Rm| ≤ r^{-2} has volume ≥ κ r^n. This property is repeatedly assumed (e.g., in Lemma 6.4.1, Lemma 6.3.1 arguments) and is used to obtain injectivity radius and compactness in blow-up limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: κ-noncollapsing is used together with curvature bounds and Hamilton compactness to pass to smooth pointed limits; it's a key hypothesis in Perelman-style blow-up/classification arguments.
